items.title: India Began Building Bridges When the World Was Building Walls: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
items.summary: He noted that India recorded USD 863 billion in exports last year and has set itself the target of achieving USD 1 trillion in exports in the current year. This would represent nearly 16 per cent growth in a year when international trade is expected to grow by only around 2.5 to 3 per cent, while the global economy remains vulnerable to shocks and global growth is expected to fall below 3 per cent.

facts.text: He noted that India recorded USD 863 billion in exports last year and has set itself the target of achieving USD 1 trillion in exports in the current year.

This would represent nearly 16 per cent growth in a year when international trade is expected to grow by only around 2.5 to 3 per cent, while the global economy remains vulnerable to shocks and global growth is expected to fall below 3 per cent.

Shri Goyal expressed confidence that India would achieve the USD 1 trillion export target, noting that the target has been set not merely by the government but by the people and businesses of India, including 63 million MSMEs, large and small industries, global capability centres and around 250,0…

He also said that the Reserve Bank of India had once again raised its growth projections for the current year and expressed confidence that India would continue to grow at over 7 per cent and remain the fastest-growing large economy.

items.title: Department of Telecommunications hosts High-Level Roundtable with State IT Ministers and Secretaries to Accelerate Digital Connectivity and Infrastructure Rollout
items.summary: The Roundtable was chaired by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, along with Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications & Rural Development, and Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications.

facts.text: A key focus of the Roundtable was the implementation of the Telecommunication (Right of Way) Rules, 2024, notified by DoT under the Telecommunications Act, 2023.

The Special Assistance for Capital Investment (SASCI) Scheme 2026–27, with an earmarked allocation of ₹4,000 crore, was also highlighted as an important enabler for strengthening implementation of RoW reforms by States and their agencies, including State PSUs, corporations and Urban Local Bodies.

The ABP is aimed at upgrading the existing BharatNet network, creating incremental network infrastructure for new Gram Panchayats (GPs), connecting non-GP villages on demand and providing 1.5 crore fibre internet connections.
As of August 2026, 55,780 km of Optical Fibre Cable had been laid and 28,700 Gram Panchayats had been upgraded and connected under ABP.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-4 › Communication networks in India - postal, telecom and digital connectivity › Regulators and bodies - TRAI, DoT, Prasar Bharati, TDSAT - functions
bullets: TRAI (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India): Basis TRAI Act, 1997; Function Regulator of telecom and broadcasting (tariffs, quality of service, recommendations on spectrum/licensing)
TDSAT (Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal): Basis Created by 2000 amendment of TRAI Act; Function Adjudicates telecom disputes; hears appeals against TRAI orders
DoT (Department of Telecommunications): Basis Under Ministry of Communications; Function Telecom policy, licensing, spectrum management, digital connectivity, telecom R&D (CDCA Jul 2026)

Ministry of I&B also regulates private TV channels and MSOs/cable operators under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995, auctions private FM channels and operationalises Community Radio Stations (IYB 2026).

Department of Posts (India Post) is the other arm of the Ministry of Communications; the Union MoS for Communications is Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar (TH, 19 Feb 2026); Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia (TH, 23 Feb 2026).

sections.topic: Telecom technologies · Optical fibre
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Telecom technologies - 3G to 5G and 6G roadmap, satellite communication, optical fibre › Optical fibre - working principle, signal form, undersea cables (CANI), national fibre targets
bullets: Works on total internal reflection; signals travel as pulses of light (LENS Sep 2025). It is the fastest data-transmission medium compared with copper cable, radio waves and satellite signals (APPSC 2025 asked).
Main use is communication; single-mode fibre carries signals over long distances, multi-mode over short runs .

Undersea cables are fibre-optic lines on the seabed, about 1.5 million km globally; optical repeaters every 60-80 km; carry nearly 99% of international internet and telecom traffic; cheaper and lower-latency than satellites (LENS Sep 2025).

National fibre: NOFN planned to link all 2,50,000 Gram Panchayats using existing PSU fibre (BSNL, RailTel, Power Grid); funded by USOF; uses GPON technology; est. cost Rs 20,000 cr (APP). NOFN was later renamed BharatNet .
Exam angle: statement sets on TIR, light signals and single-mode fibre ("All of the above").

sections.topic: Networks and the internet · Network devices and transmission
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Networks and the internet - LAN/WAN, protocols, IP, DNS, web technologies › Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre
bullets: Router: Role Connects different networks, routes by IP; OSI layer Network (3)
Modem: Role Modulator-demodulator: digital <→ analog; OSI layer Physical
Transmission modes: simplex (one way: radio/TV broadcast, keyboard), half duplex (both ways, one at a time: walkie-talkie), full duplex (both at once: telephone) .

Connections: DSL runs on the telephone copper line, cable on coaxial TV cable, fibre on light pulses in optical fibre . Satellite internet has space, ground and user (VSAT) segments and needs no terrestrial wire.

items.title: NHRC, India concludes its two-day Bihar Open Hearing and Camp Sitting in Patna
items.summary: Ramasubramanian today concluded its two-day Bihar Open Hearing and Camp sitting in Patna. The Chairperson and Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani heard more than 70 alleged cases of human rights violations in the presence of victims and concerned officers.

facts.text: The Chairperson and Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani heard more than 70 alleged cases of human rights violations in the presence of victims and concerned officers.
Altogether, compensation exceeding Rs. 1 crore was reported as disbursed, marking a significant step in ensuring justice and redress for human rights violations.
In another case involving the rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl in Maner area of District Patna, the Commission recommended payment of Rs. 5 lakh as relief to the next of kin (NoK) of the victim.
In two other cases of death in judicial custody, the Commission observed negligence of jail/ medical officials and recommended relief of Rs.15 lakh.

facts.text: 08 OCT 2026 1:12PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, represented India at the 20th East Asia Summit Energy Ministers’ Meeting held in Manila, Philippines, today.

He also recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s announcement at the 22nd ASEAN India Summit in 2025 to support the ASEAN Power Grid initiative through training of 400 professionals on grid connectivity.

items.title: Rupee may be undervalued, markets can be irrational: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra
items.summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra indicated that the rupee is undervalued and the central bank will intervene. The rupee closed at 96.78, down 36 paise from the previous day, hitting a five-month low. Malhotra mentioned that global AI stock corrections could attract foreign capital to India. Despite a robust services trade surplus, the current account deficit has widened due to increased merchandise trade deficit.

items.summary: The document was recently released by Shri Nitin Gadkari, Hon’ble Minister for Road Transport and Highways during Chintan Shivir held in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat. The document reflects NHAI’s approach towards developing National Highway infrastructure that balances requirements of connectivity and mobility with environmental sustainability and wildlife conservation.

facts.text: Over last five years, around Rs. 19,700 crores have been invested in wildlife mitigation infrastructure and related environmental protection measures across National Highway projects.
NHAI’s mitigation planning is guided by the ecological sensitivity of project corridors, wildlife movement patterns and the technical feasibility of infrastructure design.

As part of the structural mitigation measures, around Rs. 4,600 crores have been invested in animal underpasses, Rs. 650 crores in animal overpasses, Rs. 8,300 crores in viaducts, Rs. 2,800 crores in tunnels, Rs. 2,500 crores in major bridges and Rs. 500 crores in minor bridges.

To guide wildlife towards designated crossing structures and reduce the possibility of animal–vehicle conflicts, guide fencing and noise barriers have been provided at over 300 km of National Highway alignments.

items.title: As part of ‘Khadi Festival-2026’ at I.N.A. KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel inaugurated a special Khadi and Village Industries Exhibition at Delhi Haat
items.summary: The exhibition, which will be held till October 15, 2026 has a total of 115 stalls. Of these, 48 stalls belong to Khadi while the remaining stalls belong to entrepreneurs and artisans belonging to Gramodyog & PMEGP units. Artisans, Khadi institutions, village industries units and entrepreneurs from almost every part of the country have displayed their products here.

facts.text: The inaugural function was attended by the CEO of KVIC, Joint Secretary (ARI) of the Ministry of MSME, Financial Advisor of KVIC, officers, employees, representatives of Khadi institutions and artisans.

Chairman KVIC Shri Goel said that Khadi and village industries are not just a medium of selling products but inherit a saga of hard work, skill and self-reliance of millions of artisans, weavers and rural entrepreneurs.
The turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector stood at over Rs 1.87 lakh crore in the financial year 2025-26, while more than 2.04 crore people are getting employment through this sector.
He expressed confidence that the sector will also achieve the turnover target of Rs 2.51 lakh crore in the coming time.

bullets: The biggest drawback of a multi-rate structure is misclassification of goods and services (APPSC-G1 2017 key): near-identical products fall in different slabs, inviting disputes and litigation; LENS (Aug 2025) listed "standardise product classification" among pending reforms.
Inverted Duty Structure (IDS): tax rate on inputs > tax rate on output, so input tax credit piles up and working capital is blocked; the law allows refund of unutilised ITC in such cases.
GST 2.0 (NextGen GST reforms): approved by the 56th GST Council meeting, 3-4 September 2025; effective 22 September 2025.

bullets: Categories: (1) 100% automatic (civil aviation MRO, ports, railway infrastructure); (2) Government route up to 100% (multi-brand retail, satellites); (3) automatic up to a cap, approval beyond (private banks); (4) fixed cap only.

Automatic route: no prior approval of RBI or Government; only post-facto reporting to RBI. Government route: prior approval of the concerned Ministry through the Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal (FIFP).

Prohibited: lottery; gambling and betting (including casinos); chit funds; Nidhi companies; trading in TDRs; real estate business and farmhouses; manufacture of cigars/cigarettes of tobacco; atomic energy; railway operations (other than permitted activities) .

Trade balance favoured India until the mid-18th century; decline came with Aurangzeb's Deccan wars, insecurity and loss of Indian shipping.

bullets: Held by banks themselves (not deposited with RBI) as cash, gold, unencumbered G-secs/T-bills/SDLs and approved securities (APP; CDI; UPSC).
Shortfall penalty: bank rate + 3% a year, rising to bank rate + 5% if the shortfall continues (APP).

sections.topic: Inflation types
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures › Inflation types - definition and causes
bullets: Food: Meaning / cause Rise in food prices (CFPI) - monsoon, supply shocks
Cost-push: Meaning / cause Input costs (wages, raw materials, fuel) rise, supply falls, prices go up
Export-led: Meaning / cause Strong export demand drains domestic supply and pushes prices up
Skewflation: Meaning / cause Prices rise in a few commodities (e.g. food) while others stay stable

Supply shocks dominate: erratic monsoon and El Niño (vegetables), crude oil prices, rupee depreciation; the West Asia conflict pushed up fuel and input costs in 2026 (TH, 13 Mar and 20 Apr 2026; CDCA Jul 2026).

facts.text: Launched on 18 October 2016 , the National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme provides focused support to enterprises across different stages of their growth journey.
It has also contributed to a significant expansion in procurement from SC/ST Owned MSEs, which increased nearly 39-fold from ₹99.37 crore in 2015-16 to ₹4,013.42 crore in 2025-26.

sections.topic: Access and benefit sharing
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 22 › Biodiversity hotspots in India; endemism; Biological Diversity Act 2002 and access-benefit sharing › Access and benefit sharing - benefit-sharing cases (Kani tribe, Arogyapacha)
bullets: ABS means commercial benefits from bioresources are shared with the communities that provide them. It covers plant, animal and microbial resources and traditional knowledge, but excludes human genetic material. The CBD introduced it in 1992 and the Nagoya Protocol put it into operation in 2010.

Kani model : the Kani tribe of Kerala shared knowledge of Arogyapacha (Trichopus zeylanicus). TBGRI, Thiruvananthapuram, used it to develop the anti-fatigue drug "Jeevani" and shared the licence fee and royalty with a Kani trust. It was the first well-known benefit-sharing model.
NBA's ABS has raised over ₹266 crore since 2008. Red Sanders accounts for 45% (₹120 crore) of that and the seed sector for 32.3% (LENSD, 26 Jun 2026).

New fund rules (NBA): if a resource comes from an identifiable repository, 25-40% of ABS funds go to it and 60-75% go to local communities through SBBs/UTBCs. If the origin cannot be traced, the money goes to conservation (VIS Apr 2026). India also notified ABS Regulations 2025, which cover Digital Sequence Information (APPCA).

APSBB plans a first-of-its-kind Marine ABS framework for fishermen and will strengthen about 13,000 BMCs (TH, 30 Apr 2026). NBA sanctioned ₹82 lakh to APSBB for Red Sanders conservation (LENS Oct 2025).

bullets: Art 79: Parliament = President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha (Arts 79-122, Part V).

President is part of Parliament though not a member: no bill becomes law without assent; he summons, prorogues, dissolves, addresses and promulgates ordinances - like the "Crown-in-Parliament" in the UK; contrast the US (CDI).

He does not sit in Parliament; Art. 86 lets him address either House or both; Art. 87 special address to both Houses at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year (VIS PT365 2026).

bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .

sections.topic: Mobility through reservation, education, migration
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Social stratification and mobility in India › Mobility through reservation, education, migration
bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

sections.topic: Transgender persons · Reservation and state measures
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-5 › Transgender persons - NALSA judgment, Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019 › Reservation and state measures - horizontal vs vertical, first service quota, AP pensions, welfare board, ID cards
bullets: Debate: NALSA (2014) asked governments to treat transgender persons as socially and educationally backward (a vertical OBC-type quota); the community seeks horizontal reservation cutting across SC/ST/OBC/General. The issue resurfaced in June 2023 with a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra's reply to the Bombay High Court (APPSC 2022).
Karnataka - first State to give 1% reservation to transgender persons in all government services (July 2021) (APPSC 2023).

The state's "One Family-One Entrepreneur" policy targets 5 lakh women entrepreneurs (TH, Jan 2026).

sections.topic: Feminisation of agriculture
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-2 › Rural credit and rural non-farm sector; migration and rural distress › Feminisation of agriculture - meaning and causes
bullets: Meaning: rising share of women in the agricultural workforce (as cultivators, labourers and unpaid family workers) while men move to non-farm and urban work.

Causes: male out-migration to cities; distress - low household income pushes rural women into low-productivity farm work; concentration of women in subsistence farming and unpaid family work (LENSD, 24 Aug 2026); COVID-era return migration made women intensify farm work (TH, 25 Jul 2026).

Data: rural FLFPR (15+) rose 33.0% → 45.9% vs urban 23.3% → 27.7% (2019-20 to 2025); overall FLFPR 30% → 40%; rural women = 80% of the rise in female workers 2017-18 to 2023-24 (PLFS, LENSD 24 Aug 2026).
Women's WPR follows a U-shaped curve (Claudia Goldin): high in agriculture in the 1980s, fell with mechanisation 2004-05 to 2012, rising again after 2020 partly out of distress (TH, 25 Jul 2026).

sections.topic: Occupational structure of India
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-1 › Occupational structure of India - trends and inter-state variation › Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences
bullets: 72.4% of India's workers lived in rural areas (APPSC-GS 2025) , against 68.8% of the population.
Female workers: 55% agricultural labourers, 24% cultivators; women hold only 12.8% of operational holdings → feminisation of agriculture (UPSC notes).
Quality (PLFS 2025): regular wage/salaried share 22% → 24%, self-employment 58% → 56% (TH, 15 May 2026); rural women workers self-employed 60% (2011-12) → 73% (2023-24) (TH, 12 Mar 2026).
Rural women gave 80% of the rise in female workers (2017-18 to 2023-24); feminisation of agriculture driven by subsistence farming, unpaid family work and distress employment.

Norm: population 500+ in plains; 250+ in hill States, NE, deserts and Schedule V/tribal areas; 100+ in LWE-affected blocks.
Phases: PMGSY-I (2000), PMGSY-II (2013, upgradation), RCPLWEA (2016, LWE roads), PMGSY-III (2019, through routes and major rural links).

bullets: New insurance model announced May 2025 by Health Minister Y. Satya Kumar Yadav: cover up to ₹25 lakh per family per year for about 1.65 crore poor and middle-class families (APPSC PYQs).

108 emergency service: 768 ambulances, 9.22 lakh patients transported (APSES 2024-25); 108 and Aarogyasri are YSR-era schemes (TH, 9 Jul 2026). 104: mobile medical units giving fixed-day village health services .

Model change: under the Universal Health Policy, every citizen gets free treatment up to ₹2.5 lakh (insurance mode), and the poor get treatment up to ₹25 lakh through the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust (TH, 1 Mar 2026). The G2-GS 2024 statement that the new insurance model covers up to ₹25 lakh per family a year was keyed correct.
EHS (Employees Health Scheme): cashless treatment for State government employees and pensioners through the same Trust .
Health budget 2026-27: ₹19,305 crore (TH, 1 Mar 2026); AP MMR 45, IMR 24 (APSES).

sections.topic: ESI and EPF
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-6 › Important flagship programmes of the Central Government - social sector (health, education, nutrition, housing) › ESI and EPF - establishments covered, wage ceiling, contribution rates, benefits
bullets: EPF: 12% of wages from employee and employer (10% for notified establishments) (LENSD, 4 Jul 2026). Covers establishments with 20+ employees .

EPF Scheme, 2026 replaced the EPF Scheme 1952 under the Code on Social Security. Members carry over automatically; voluntary contributions above the ceiling are allowed; the principal employer is liable for contract workers' PF; linking Aadhaar, PAN and UAN is mandatory (LENSD, 4 Jul 2026).

Wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage raised from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a month (Cabinet, LENSD 17 Sep 2026). The ₹15,000 ceiling dated from Sep 2014; the change is expected to add 51 lakh+ employees. Benefits: PF, EPS pension, EDLI insurance.

ESI (ESI Act 1948): ceiling ₹21,000 a month; employer 3.25%, employee 0.75%; medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and dependants' benefits . Under the SS Code, ESIC coverage is pan-India (CDI); SPREE (Jul 2025-Jan 2026) added 1.03 crore employees (TH, 17 Jan 2026).

sections.topic: Banking in India · Bank nationalisation
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Banking in India - nationalisation, structure, priority sector, small finance and payments banks › Bank nationalisation - rounds, year, number, chronology
bullets: 1955: Event SBI Act: Imperial Bank became SBI, the first public sector bank; RBI bought 92% of its shares (APP)

1969 banks and their fate: Allahabad (now Indian Bank), BoB, BoI, BoM, Central, Canara, Dena (now BoB), Indian Bank, IOB, PNB, Syndicate (now Canara), UCO, Union, United Bank of India (now PNB) (APP).

1980 banks: Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank (both now Union Bank), Oriental Bank of Commerce (now PNB), Punjab & Sind Bank, Vijaya Bank (now BoB), New Bank of India . APP lists five and prints "Oriental Bank of India".
Motives: social control of credit and a shift of credit to agriculture and small industry (APP; APPCA). The Lead Bank Scheme began the same year, 1969. The 50th anniversary was 19 July 2019.
Reasons: industrial houses controlled banks; agriculture and small units were neglected. Results: branch expansion and priority-sector lending.

sections.topic: Banking sector reforms · Privatisation debate
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Banking sector reforms - Narasimham Committee I and II, Basel norms, bank mergers, privatisation debate › Privatisation debate - IDBI Bank, Banking Laws Amendment, PSB privatisation
bullets: IDBI Bank: LIC bought a majority stake in 2019, so RBI reclassified it as a private lender. The Government and LIC are selling a combined 60.72% strategic stake (CDI).
Minority stake sales were weighed in UCO, BoM, Central Bank, Punjab & Sind and IOB to meet minimum public shareholding (CDI).
Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, in force from 1 Aug 2025, made 19 amendments across the RBI Act, BR Act, SBI Act and the Banking Companies Acts of 1970 and 1980 (LENS Aug 2025).
"Substantial interest" threshold raised from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore; co-operative bank directors' tenure from 8 to 10 years; unclaimed PSB shares can go to the IEPF.
AITUC called it a "clear call to privatisation" of PSBs (TH 2 Feb 2026).

Fewest post offices: Visakhapatnam (156-158); rural districts have more branch POs (CDI, SES 2025-26).

Rural districts have more branch post offices (universal service); urban districts fewer. AP has 14.98 commercial bank branches per lakh population vs Goa 43.31 (SDG India Index 2023-24).

bullets: Banking Regulation Act, 1949: licensing, branch opening, management, amalgamation, cash reserve and liquidity (SLR), audit and inspection of banks; payments banks licensed under Sec. 22(1) (e.g. IPPB, 2018).

NBFCs regulated under Chapter IIIB of the RBI Act ; RBI Ombudsman: RB-IOS 2026 from 1 July 2026 - "One Nation One Ombudsman" for banks, RRBs, UCBs, NBFCs and payment operators; no cap on dispute amount.
DEA Fund (2014, Sec. 26A BR Act): unclaimed deposits of 10+ years; the depositor's right survives.
Not in your sources: the current list of States whose banking business RBI does not conduct.

sections.topic: Party system in India · Consequences of coalition politics
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Party system in India - one-party dominance, multi-party and coalition eras › Consequences of coalition politics - stability, federalism, role of parties
bullets: Increased role of regional and small parties - the APPSC-keyed "major consequence".
Consensus building, but slow decisions; policy reversals/delays; compromises dilute strong measures (CDI).
Checks and balances: no single party holds absolute power; regional representation in national policy (CDI).
Defections and horse-trading led to the anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule, 52nd Amendment, 1985) - the first time parties entered the Constitution.
Federalism became more bargained after 1989 (APP).

sections.topic: Indian political parties · Party concepts
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Indian political parties - evolution, ideology and classification › Party concepts - inner-party democracy, party system, social bases of parties, Kamaraj Plan
bullets: one-party dominance or the "Congress system" (1952-77);
India is a multi-party system because it divides along region, language, caste, religion and class.
Social bases: caste, region/language, religion and class. Regional parties rose on identity; for example, the TDP took power within 9 months on "Telugu atma gauravam".
Party problems listed: money power, criminalisation (Vohra Committee 1993), casteism, defections, weak ideology.
Kamaraj Plan (1963): senior Congress ministers resigned to work in the party organisation .

sections.topic: Caste in modern India · Caste and politics
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Caste in modern India - dominant caste, sanskritisation, caste associations, caste and politics › Caste and politics - vote banks, caste parties, politicisation of caste (Rajni Kothari)
bullets: Rajni Kothari edited *Caste in Indian Politics* (1970) ; his *Politics in India* links identities to electoral mobilisation (CDX).
The colonial roots run from the Minto-Morley Reforms 1909 (separate electorates) through vote-bank politics built on caste associations (APP).
Christophe Jaffrelot, *India's Silent Revolution*: the rise of lower castes through politics (CDX).
The conflict now is for power, not ritual status, and casteism in politics has increased (CDX).
Exam angle: RPSC 2013 A-R. Castes are being politicised, and casteism in politics is increasing. Both are true, but R is not the explanation.

sections.topic: Laws for women · Dowry Prohibition Act 1961
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-5 › Laws for women - Dowry Prohibition Act, Domestic Violence Act 2005, POSH Act 2013, Maternity Benefit Amendment › Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections
bullets: Dowry (s.2): property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, before, at or any time after marriage in connection with it; excludes dower/mahr .
s.8B: Offence / provision Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Govt
Definition (Section 2): property or valuable security given, or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, in connection with a marriage. Mahr under Muslim personal law is excluded .
Offences are cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable; the burden of proof lies on the accused; states appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers .
